old: one newly inundated area A_new: every cell outside the normal regime counted alike, the reed beds above the normal surface included; corridor 7 June median {{T12|region=DNIPRO_CORRIDOR,date=2023-06-07|A_p50_km2||.1f}} km2

reason: the reed beds were wet emergent vegetation before the breach -- in spring 2023 the normally-wet reed beds and the reed beds that the event alone reaches share a C-band double-bounce signature that the reed beds above its reach lack, and a normal June shows no optical water on them (T12i) -- and neither optical water indices nor C-band see water under the canopy (Lefebvre et al. 2019; Slagter et al. 2020); reference-water practice (Martinis et al. 2022)
impact_on_conclusion: A_new, W_total and V_new are unchanged; the new flooding of dry ground is the part of A_new that observations can confirm or refute; over the wetland the event extent agrees with UNOSAT (a diagnostic, largely prevalence: T16b) while the attribution of the inundated wetland to new versus seasonally wet ground depends on the reconstructed pre-breach state, whose nominal value lies above its Monte-Carlo interval
